first_line_rotterdam.title: First-Line Rotterdam Diagnostic Criteria
first_line_rotterdam.description: According to the Rotterdam Consensus (2003/2018), a formal diagnosis of PCOS requires meeting at least 2 of the 3 key criteria below.

criteria.label: Hyperandrogenism (High Testosterone or Clinical Symptoms)
criteria.description: High total/free testosterone in blood report (> 45 ng/dL), or clinical signs like moderate-to-severe acne or facial hair (hirsutism).

criteria.label: Ovulatory Dysfunction (Irregular Menstrual Cycles)
criteria.description: Cycle length <21 days or >35 days, or fewer than 9 cycles per year.

criteria.label: Polycystic Ovaries on Ultrasound
criteria.description: Presence of >=20 follicles per ovary or an ovarian volume >=10 mL on pelvic ultrasound.

exclusion_criteria.title: Clinical Exclusion Criteria Notice
exclusion_criteria.description: To ensure diagnostic accuracy and avoid false secondary signals, the following secondary disorders must be ruled out by your healthcare provider:
conditions: Thyroid Dysfunction (checked via TSH: 0.4–4.0 µIU/mL to rule out primary hypo/hyperthyroidism)
Hyperprolactinemia (checked via Serum Prolactin: <25 ng/mL to rule out prolactinoma)
Non-Classic Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (NCAH: checked via 17-OHP <200 ng/dL to rule out 21-hydroxylase deficiency)
Cushing's Syndrome or Adrenal Tumors (checked via 24h Cortisol to rule out adrenal hypersecretion)

metabolic.label: Metabolic PCOS (Insulin Resistant / Dysmetabolic)
metabolic.description: Characterized by impaired glucose tolerance, insulin resistance, elevated triglycerides, and visceral weight storage.

questions.label: Height & Weight (BMI Calculation)
questions.reference: Asian BMI threshold >= 23.0 kg/m² indicates overweight/obesity classification

questions.label: Do you have darkened, velvety skin patches on your neck, armpits, or groin (Acanthosis Nigricans)?
Lipid Profile: Triglycerides & HDL (mg/dL)
questions.reference: Triglyceride to HDL ratio > 3.0 indicates atherogenic dyslipidemia & insulin resistance

hormonal.label: Hormonal PCOS (Ovarian / Androgen Excess)
hormonal.description: Driven by ovarian hyperandrogenism, altered gonadotropin pulsatility, and elevated testosterone.

questions.label: LH to FSH Ratio
questions.reference: LH:FSH ratio >= 2.0 reflects aberrant hypothalamic-pituitary gonadotropin secretion

questions.label: Sex Hormone-Binding Globulin (SHBG nmol/L)
questions.reference: Low SHBG (< 30 nmol/L) increases free bioavailable testosterone

adrenal.label: Adrenal PCOS (HPA-Axis & Stress Driven)
adrenal.description: Promoted by hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal overactivation and elevated adrenal androgen production.

questions.label: DHEA-S (Dehydroepiandrosterone Sulfate µg/dL)
questions.reference: Primary marker for adrenal androgen production (> 350 µg/dL)

questions.label: Perceived Stress Scale (PSQ: 1 = Low Stress, 10 = Severe Daily Stress)
questions.reference: PSQ score >= 7/10 reflects chronic HPA-axis activation

questions.label: Do you experience poor sleep quality or less than 6 hours of sleep?
questions.reference: Circadian rhythm disruption raises nocturnal cortisol & DHEA-S

inflammatory.label: Inflammatory PCOS (Gut Dysbiosis & Chronic Inflammation)
inflammatory.description: Driven by systemic low-grade inflammation, gut mucosal permeability, and immune activation.

questions.label: High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein (hs-CRP mg/L)
questions.reference: hs-CRP > 3.0 mg/L indicates systemic low-grade inflammation

questions.label: Do you frequently experience bloating, constipation, IBS, or food intolerances?
questions.reference: Gastrointestinal permeability and endotoxemia disrupt steroidogenesis

questions.label: Serum Vitamin D3 (25-OH Vitamin D ng/mL)
questions.reference: Vitamin D deficiency (< 20 ng/mL) impairs immune tolerance & insulin sensitivity

mitochondrial_axis.label: Energy & Cellular Health Screen
mitochondrial_axis.description: Evaluates cellular energy deficits, sluggishness, and tissue hypoxia triggers.

questions.label: Do you experience persistent daytime fatigue, sluggishness, or brain fog?
Do you experience sleep apnea, heavy snoring, or waking up gasping for air?
questions.reference: Intermittent nocturnal hypoxia disrupts ovarian follicle development

questions.label: Do you feel shallow breathing, air hunger, or shortness of breath easily?
Do you experience post-exertional malaise or severe crash after light exercise?

questions.label: Describe your menstrual cycle history (e.g. missed months, heavy bleeding, painful periods)
Perceived Stress Scale (PSQ: 1-10)
questions.definition: 1-3: Low Stress | 4-6: Moderate Stress | 7-10: High Stress (Elevated Cortisol/DHEA-S)

primary_goals: Regulate my menstrual cycles and periods
Boost daily energy & eliminate brain fog
Clear skin, acne, and reduce facial hair (hirsutism)
Support weight management & lower stubborn belly fat
Improve sleep quality & manage stress levels

medical_glossary.HOMA-IR: Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance. Calculated from fasting glucose and fasting insulin. A value > 2.0 suggests insulin resistance.
medical_glossary.DHEA-S: Dehydroepiandrosterone Sulfate. An androgen produced almost exclusively by the adrenal glands, reflecting adrenal stress response.
medical_glossary.hs-CRP: High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein. A blood biomarker indicating systemic low-grade inflammation.
medical_glossary.LH:FSH Ratio: Luteinizing Hormone to Follicle-Stimulating Hormone ratio. In healthy cycles it is 1:1; a ratio >= 2:1 is characteristic of ovarian PCOS.
medical_glossary.Acanthosis Nigricans: Darkened, velvety hyperpigmentation in skin folds (neck/axilla) caused by high circulating insulin binding to IGF receptors.
medical_glossary.Rotterdam Criteria: International clinical consensus defining PCOS by requiring at least 2 of 3 features: androgen excess, irregular cycles, or polycystic ovaries on ultrasound.

overrides.label: Isolated Adrenal Androgen Excess (DHEA-S > 350 µg/dL with normal Fasting Insulin)
overrides.reference: Section 3 Rule 1: DHEA-S elevated + Fasting Insulin normal confirms pure Adrenal phenotype.

overrides.label: Severe Insulin Resistance (Fasting Insulin > 15 µIU/mL or HOMA-IR > 2.5)
overrides.reference: Section 3 Rule 2: Severe hyperinsulinemia overrules mild symptom tallies to trigger Metabolic protocol.

overrides.label: Systemic Low-Grade Inflammation (hs-CRP > 3.0 mg/L)
overrides.reference: Section 3 Rule 3: Elevated hs-CRP confirms Inflammatory phenotype driver.

overrides.label: Classic Ovarian Hyperandrogenism (Total Testosterone > 55 ng/dL & LH:FSH >= 2.0)
overrides.reference: Section 3 Rule 4: Markedly elevated testosterone + LH:FSH >= 2.0 confirms classic Hormonal phenotype.
